title: Endogenous opioid dynamics in the dorsal striatum sculpt neural activity to promote goal-directed action
title_zh: 背侧纹状体内源性阿片动力学塑造神经活动以促进目标导向行为
abstract: Endogenous neuropeptides are uniquely poised to regulate neuronal activity and behavior across multiple timescales. Traditional studies ascribing neuropeptide contributions to behavior lack spatiotemporal precision. The endogenous opioid dynorphin is a neuropeptide highly enriched in the dorsal striatum, a region critical for goal-directed behavior. However, the functional role of endogenous dynorphin- kappa opioid receptor (KOR) signaling in goal-directed behavior is unknown. Here, we report that local, time-locked dynorphin release from dorsomedial striatum medium spiny neurons (MSNs) is necessary and sufficient for goal-directed behavior using a suite of modern approaches, including conditional deletions, neuropeptide biosensor detection, two-photon imaging, and time-locked optogenetic manipulations of neuropeptide release. We discovered that glutamatergic axon terminals from the basolateral amygdala evoke striatal dynorphin release, resulting in feed-forward retrograde presynaptic G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) inhibition to promote behavior. Collectively, our findings isolate a causal role for endogenous neuropeptide release at rapid timescales and subsequent pre-synaptic Gi-GPCR activity for promoting goal-directed behavior.
abstract_zh: 内源性神经肽在多种时间尺度上独特地调节神经元活动和行为。传统研究将神经肽对行为的贡献归因缺乏空间时间精度。内源性阿片肽多巴胺能肽在背侧纹状体高度富集，该区域对目标导向行为至关重要。然而，内源性多巴胺能肽-κ阿片受体（KOR）信号在目标导向行为中的功能角色尚不清楚。我们报告，来自背侧内侧纹状体中间棘突神经元（MSNs）的局部、时间锁定的多巴胺能肽释放是实现目标导向行为所必需且足够的，采用了一系列现代方法，包括条件缺失、神经肽生物传感器检测、双光子成像以及对神经肽释放的时间锁定光遗传操控。我们发现，来自基底外侧杏仁核的谷氨酸能轴突终端诱导纹状体多巴胺能肽释放，导致前向递归的后突触前G蛋白偶联受体（GPCR）抑制，从而促进行为。综上所述，我们的发现揭示了内源性神经肽在快速时间尺度上的因果作用以及随后前突触Gi-GPCR活性在促进目标导向行为中的作用。
